title: Glad that unauthorized recordings exist
summary: Machito says recordings with Parker, McGhee and Belafonte show people liked the music and preserved great moments.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Now that you've heard all those recordings that were taped-recorded without your knowledge like the ones with Howard McGhee and Brew Moore and Charlie Parker, are you glad that they were recorded?

Because whoever - I am a sentimentalism, now, whoever record what I am playing is because he likes what he is hearing. So, they give you a great satisfaction and maybe an incentive to keep playing the best, the best way that is possible to play, because this is a message and is a communication. I consider that music, the one that I made or whoever made it, is a communication and is a happy communication.
Macho, wouldn't you also say that had someone not recorded these, these moments, these great moments of Latin music would've been lost?
Because here someone without your knowledge recorded it, now they have perpetuated Machito with
Charlie Parker live at the Royal Roost, Machito and Howard McGhee, Machito and Harry Belafonte, Machito with John Henry Lewis, of the Modern Jazz Quartet, ahh - Do you feel that it was a good thing?
